utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Would the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is IT-04-82, the Prosecutor versus Ljube Boskoski and Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand to make this as clear as the first thing?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: May I now have the appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Bill Smith for the Prosecution with Hasan Younis as case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you. And appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Antonio Apostolski, Defence counsel of the accused Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tarculovski, on the strength of the order by Judge Agius on the 5th of April this year, the Presiding Judge of Trial Chamber II, I became the pre-trial judge. My name is Albin Eser; I come from Germany. Mr. Tarculovski, at the initial appearance conducted by Judge Agius on the 20th of March this year, you chose not to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty. According to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal, you are to be called upon to enter a plea within 30 days after the initial appearance. This is the reason why we have gathered again today to enable you to do so. First of all, I would like to remind you once more that you have the right to remain silent. That is one of your basic rights. In other words, no one can force you to answer or to say anything. Mr. Tarculovski, you are represented by Mr. Apostolski. Do you have anything to say about your being represented by this Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: No. Thank you. Mr. Tarculovski, you already confirmed at the initial appearance that you have been provided with the copy of the indictment in your own language. Now you are entitled to have a fresh reading of the indictment, in full, if you wish to do so. Do you wish to have the indictment read out to you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no need.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I think he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: There is no need to read it? No? Okay. Yes, thank you. Now pursuant to Rule 62(A), subparagraph (iii), you have the right to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty on each count of the indictment. Should you fail to enter a plea now, I shall enter a plea of not guilty on your behalf. Is this clear to you? That if you do not say anything, it will be considered as a plea of not guilty and it would have to be expressed by me. Now, Mr. Tarculovski, do you wish to enter a plea to this hearing today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please remind the accused to use the microphone because we are lipreading from the screen instead of...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Could you please get a little bit closer to the microphone because the interpreter has problems -- has a problem to hear you. Now, in view of your waiver, the whole indictment will not be read out to you. I will just read out to you the three charges contained in the indictment and then I will ask you how do you plead to that charge, guilty or not guilty. Your answer, in each case, should be guilty or not guilty, as the case may be. So you should not add anything else. Now, Mr. Tarculovski, would you please stand up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: The first count which you are charged with is a charge of murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, recognised under Article 3(I)(a) of the Geneva Convention of 1949 and punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. For this count, you are charged with individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: The second count, which you are charged with is a charge of wanton destruction of cities, towns and villages, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3(b) of the Statute of the Tribunal. For this count, you are charged with individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Okay. The third count which you are charged with is a charge of cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3(I) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 and punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. For this count, you are charged with individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask the registrar to note that Mr. Tarculovski has pleaded not guilty to the three counts of the indictment. You may sit down now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: As a result of these pleas, the registrar will take note that the trial must be fixed in due course. Now, there are some other issues perhaps to be raised. Pursuant to Rule 60 bis (A), a Status Conference is to be convened within 120 days of this initial appearance. That means around the middle of August of this year. The purpose of this Status Conference is twofold. First, to organise exchanges between the parties and facilitate expeditious Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. preparation for trial and, second, to review the status of this case and to allow the accused the opportunity to raise any issues, including his mental and physical conditions. For the time being, the accused will remain in custody. Next I would like to refer to the supporting material which accompanied the indictment against the accused. Pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i), within 30 days of the initial appearance of the accused, all the supporting material which accompanied the indictment must be made available to the Defence counsel in a language which the accused understands. The time limit is about to expire. Now, Mr. Smith, from the Prosecution, could you confirm that that disclosure of the supporting material has already been made in an appropriate form?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In relation to the disclosure of the supporting material, the Prosecution will be able to meet that deadline. However, on the last occasion Judge Agius stated the initial appearance was continuing and that would affect in fact the disclosure date of the supporting material. He stated that the 30 days would start in fact from today and finish in 30 days time. As it occurs, Mr. Boskoski, the co-accused, has been before this court on the 31st of March and will providing the supporting material within 30 days from the 31st of March and, at the same time, we'll be able to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: 31st of March?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: He appeared -- sorry, he appeared on the 1st of April. My apologies, Your Honour. And at the same time we would provide the supporting material to this accused which would be by -- I think it's by the 1st of May. It is a little bit confusing, the fact that Judge Agius had said previously that the initial appearance would be continuing. But he did explicitly state at the last hearing that the 30 days would start from this date, the finish of the initial appearance. We would -- we would have provided the supporting material before this date in any event. However, the translation of the material has been quite an extensive exercise. As Your Honour is aware, there was about 1.000 pages of material supporting the indictment, and the translation services have been working as fast as they can. And so I would ask that that interpretation be taken from Judge Agius's hearing in relation to the time that we have to provide the supporting material to the accused. But I do admit it is a bit confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now just to make it clear, what would be the really final date, according to your own...

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: It would be -- final date in relation to Mr. Tarculovski would be 30 days from now. However, as Mr. Boskoski appeared here on the 1st of April, we would supply the supporting material to both accused by the 1st of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: May I ask the Defence. Would that be agreeable to you? It would still not be 30 days from now as it was suggested by Judge Agius in the first initial appearance, but it would be even earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence agrees to have the documentation disclosed by 1st of May, and if there are problems with translation of the materials, it is possible that be received in English as well. So this is what concerns me as a Defence lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: But now, of course, we are also obliged to make it -- put the accused in a position to read it. So perhaps you could agree in this way, that at least until the May 1st, it will be disclosed and transmitted in English and then later on it should be made also accessible to the accused. Would that be agreeable to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's agreeable. But I do believe that the supporting material would be provided in both languages by that date. I've been given that confirmation by the translation services so we should be able to meet that obligation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: That would be even better. I thank you very much for your cooperation. Thank you. Thank you very much. Now, relating to the issue of this disclosure, the Defence counsel has a 30-day period for filing any preliminary motion pursuant to Rule 72(A). Once it has received all the supporting material, the 30-day time limit has commenced running since that date, but it will now run from the date which we have just fixed, which will be the 1st of May. Now, I am aware of the preliminary motion filed by the Defence counsel on March 31, 2005. As you already know, as the Prosecution had time to file a response to this, the response has been -- just arrived and so far I didn't have a chance to go through it, but you can be sure that I will take care of it as soon as I am in a position to do so and then you will get a further order in this respect. Okay? Now, is there any other matter, that you wish to raise at this stage of the proceeding?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any matter which the Defence wants to raise at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the time being, not. For the time being, we don't have anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I would like to ask the accused: Since you are detained in the detention unit, as far as being detained, is everything all right? Are you treated in a proper manner?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Ladies and gentlemen, that brings us to the end of this appearance. We will now adjourn the appearance to another day. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: adjourned at 9.20 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
